affiliations.date_precision: commissioned in the Army Air Forces on July 4, 1942; promoted to first lieutenant and then captain; detached to OSS in spring 1945

Birch as a 14th Air Force intelligence officer assigned to OSS Secret Intelligence; the Air Force Association article explicitly describes detached service. Military assignment is not classified as civilian employment.

affiliations.date_precision: began paid missionary work in July 1940; later served as a civilian chaplain before his July 4, 1942 Army Air Forces commission
affiliations.research_notes: The named organization, China assignment, start month, and monthly pay are explicit. Mercer independently corroborates Birch's missionary activity. The evidence strongly bounds this as his last identified civilian employment before military service.

affiliations.date_precision: Mercer records class year 1939; exact attendance dates were not reviewed
affiliations.research_notes: Mercer is an educational affiliation and is not classified as Birch's employer.

affiliations.role_title: Chief engineer; head of the technical commission

claims.claim_text: The indexed First Lieutenant John M. Birch is strongly matched to John Morrison Birch, the missionary and Fourteenth Air Force intelligence officer assigned to OSS in China.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The index name and grade align with the NPS exact middle initial, Fourteenth Air Force and OSS assignment, and the Air Force Association's full name and first-lieutenant promotion chronology.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the exact first name, surname, middle initial, compatible indexed grade, explicit Fourteenth Air Force-to-OSS pathway, and unusually specific China chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources sequence missionary work from July 1940, Army Air Forces commissioning in July 1942, later first-lieutenant and captain promotions, and OSS assignment in 1945.
claims.match_notes: Box 57 remains unreviewed, so the private officer identifier and exact OSS transfer order still require archival confirmation.

claims.claim_text: Birch's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was Fourteenth Air Force service as an intelligence officer.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Birch was put on detached service with the new organization.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS identifies Birch as a Fourteenth Air Force intelligence officer assigned to OSS Secret Intelligence; the Air Force Association article explicitly says he was detached to OSS in spring 1945.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the exact-name, middle-initial, grade, China, Air Force, and OSS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate military pathway from the Fourteenth Air Force into detached OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The role is a military assignment, not a civilian employer. The accessible sources differ in whether they describe assignment or detached service, but both establish the same immediate pathway.

claims.claim_text: Birch's best-supported last civilian employer before Army Air Forces service was the World Fundamentalism Missionary Fellowship, which assigned him to China.
claims.evidence_excerpt: began work in July 1940 at $50 per month.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Air Force Association article names the fellowship, China assignment, July 1940 start, and monthly pay, then sequences civilian chaplain duties and the July 1942 military commission; Mercer independently identifies Birch as a missionary.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the full-name and Fourteenth Air Force-to-OSS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded as the last identified paid civilian work before his July 4, 1942 military commission; the source does not use the phrase last civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: The claim is limited to the best-supported last identified civilian employer. Mercer is corroborative and is not treated as an employer.

claims.claim_text: Birch was a Mercer University student and member of the class of 1939 before his missionary assignment.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Mercer's official alumni page gives the 1939 class year; the Air Force Association article independently identifies him as a Mercer graduate.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same full-name, missionary, China, and wartime chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar education before the July 1940 missionary assignment; exact attendance dates are not established.
claims.match_notes: Mercer is shown only as a student affiliation, never as an employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Lieutenant Colonel Willis H. Bird is strongly matched to the Willis Bird who served as deputy chief of OSS Detachment 202 in China.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact distinctive first name and surname, indexed lieutenant-colonel grade, NPS Detachment 202 deputy-chief role, and Rider's lieutenant-colonel Eagle-team chronology align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the uncommon name, exact commissioned grade, China theater, Detachment 202 leadership, and Eagle-team command.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official source places him in Detachment 202 in early 1945; the secondary study places him commanding the Eagle team in August 1945.
claims.match_notes: Box 57 remains unreviewed and must confirm the middle initial and private officer identifier.

claims.claim_text: A secondary historical study reports that, before the war, Willis Bird was a Sears, Roebuck executive in Pennsylvania and New York.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Prior to the war he had served as an executive for Sears, Roebuck
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Rider names Sears, Roebuck, the executive role, and Pennsylvania and New York, but supplies no exact dates or direct transition into wartime service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence that the passage concerns the indexed lieutenant colonel because it describes the same uncommon name, exact grade, and OSS China role corroborated by NPS.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented only as prior to the war. It is not established as the immediate pre-OSS affiliation or last civilian employer before service.
claims.match_notes: This qualified claim is excluded from default high-confidence employer analytics. Sears or Wharton archival records are needed to establish dates and role details.

claims.claim_text: The indexed P-5 Sidney H. Birdseye is strongly matched to survey engineer Sidney H. Birdseye, chief of the Guatemala-Honduras boundary commission.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Two official sources use the exact uncommon full name and document a professional survey-engineering leadership role compatible with the index's P-5 professional grade.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the exceptionally distinctive exact name, the compatible professional grade, and two independent official records of the same engineering assignment.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official records document the role in 1935 and 1936, before wartime OSS service; they do not establish the later OSS chronology.
claims.match_notes: Box 57 is required to confirm the personnel-file linkage and explain the transition from surveying work to OSS.

claims.claim_text: In 1935-1936, Sidney H. Birdseye served as chief engineer and head of the technical commission demarcating the Guatemala-Honduras frontier.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Mr. Sidney H. Birdseye, Head of the Technical Commission
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary Coast and Geodetic Survey bulletin names Birdseye as chief engineer, and the 1936 official minutes name and record his signature as head of the technical commission.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the exact uncommon full name and compatible professional grade.
claims.temporal_assessment: Definite prewar government assignment, but not shown to be the immediate pre-OSS affiliation or last civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: The bilateral commission is classified as a government assignment, not private employment. Box 57 is needed for the later chronology.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Technician Third Grade Ralph R. Birdsall is confirmed against the official Army enlistment bulk file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The private identifier and exact full name match in the OSS index and official Army bulk file; the Army record dates entry to January 27, 1941 and records private as the entry grade.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by an exact private-identifier and full-name match, with compatible enlisted status.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army record establishes entry on January 27, 1941 but does not identify an employer or the later OSS transfer.
claims.match_notes: The full private identifier is withheld. An unverified coded field is not interpreted or published as an occupation.
